tagline: Africa's diplomatic capital — home of the AU, the fossil 'Lucy', the continent's biggest market, and the world's original coffee.
overview: Addis Ababa — 'new flower' — is Africa's diplomatic capital: the African Union's headquarters sits here, and so does one of humanity's oldest ancestors. 'Lucy,' the 3.2-million-year-old australopithecine, is the star of the National Museum.

The city runs on two fuels: coffee (Ethiopia is the plant's birthplace — the ceremony of roasting, grinding and pouring is sacred) and injera, the sour flatbread that anchors every meal. The Merkato is reputedly Africa's largest open-air market.
Speed's 2025 Africa tour streamed from Addis Ababa. The city sits at 2,400m in the Entoto foothills — springlike air, mountain views, and the gateway to Lalibela's rock churches.

funFacts.title: LUCY LIVES HERE
funFacts.text: The 3.2-million-year-old fossil — our most famous ancestor — is kept at the National Museum.

funFacts.title: AFRICA'S CAPITAL
funFacts.text: The African Union and UN Economic Commission for Africa are both headquartered here.

funFacts.title: COFFEE'S HOMELAND
funFacts.text: Ethiopia is where coffee originated — the ceremony is a daily ritual.

funFacts.title: MERKATO
funFacts.text: The sprawling open-air market is often called Africa's largest.

funFacts.title: A NEW FLOWER
funFacts.text: 'Addis Ababa' means new flower — founded in 1886 as the imperial capital.

funFacts.title: HOLY TRINITY
funFacts.text: The cathedral holds Haile Selassie's tomb — the last emperor of the Solomonic line.

funFacts.title: 2,400 METRES UP
funFacts.text: The city's altitude gives it springlike weather on the equator's edge.

funFacts.title: NEVER COLONIZED
funFacts.text: Ethiopia is the only African country never formally colonized — Addis is its proof.

funFacts.title: INJERA CULTURE
funFacts.text: The sourdough flatbread is plate and utensil at once.

funFacts.title: LALIBELA GATEWAY
funFacts.text: The rock-hewn churches — 'the new Jerusalem' — are the side trip everyone takes.

faq.q: What is the population of Addis Ababa?
faq.a: The greater Addis Ababa area is home to about 5,500,000 people.
